question:
The most common Harappan seals were ___ in shape.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: rectangular
circular
square
hexagonal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is square

Explanation:
The Harappan seals (2600-1900 BCE) were predominantly square in shape. Made of steatite, these seals featured intricate carvings of animals (e.g., bull, elephant, rhinoceros) and religious symbols like the Pashupati Seal (depicting a yogic figure). These seals were likely used for trade or ritual purposes, with inscriptions in the undeciphered Indus script.

Extra Facts:
The Harappan script remains unreadable despite numerous attempts. Seals found in Mesopotamia indicate trade links. Some seals depict a unicorn-like creature, showcasing the creativity of Harappan artisans.

question_hi:
सबसे आम हड़प्पा मुहर_____ आकार में थे।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: आयताकार
गोलाकार
वर्गाकार
षट्कोणीय
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है वर्गाकार

Explanation:
हड़प्पा सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) की मुहरें मुख्यतः वर्गाकार आकार में पाई गई हैं। ये मुहरें साबुन के पत्थर (स्टीटाइट) से बनी होती थीं और इन पर विभिन्न पशुओं (जैसे बैल, हाथी, गैंडा) व धार्मिक प्रतीकों की नक्काशी की जाती थी। इन मुहरों का उपयोग संभवतः व्यापारिक लेन-देन या धार्मिक अनुष्ठानों में किया जाता था। पशुपति मुहर (योगी की आकृति वाली मुहर) सबसे प्रसिद्ध है।

Extra Facts:
हड़प्पा मुहरों पर लिखी लिपि अभी तक पूरी तरह अपठनीय है। ये मुहरें मेसोपोटामिया जैसी अन्य सभ्यताओं से व्यापारिक संबंधों का भी प्रमाण देती हैं। कुछ मुहरों पर एकश्रृंगी पशु (यूनिकॉर्न) की आकृति भी मिलती है, जो हड़प्पावासियों की कल्पनाशीलता को दर्शाती है।

question:
Which of the following was NOT found in the Harappan excavation sites?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Dwelling houses
Public bath
Public hospital
Public buildings
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public hospital

Explanation:
The Harappan Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) was an advanced urban culture where dwelling houses, public baths (e.g., the 'Great Bath' of Mohenjo-Daro), and public buildings (e.g., granaries) have been excavated. However, no evidence of public hospitals has been found. The Harappans were pioneers in sanitation and town planning, but there is no direct proof of medical facilities.

Extra Facts:
The Harappan Civilization is also called the Indus Valley Civilization. It was known for its trade, seals, and standardized weights and measures. Harappans belonged to the Bronze Age and used a script that remains undeciphered. Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa are its major sites.

☛ Granaries - Large buildings for grain storage in Harappa

☛ Dholavira - Located in Gujarat, famous for water management
☛ Mohenjo-Daro - 'Mound of the Dead', located in Sindh (Pakistan)
question_hi:
हड़प्पा के उत्खनन स्थलों में निम्नलिखित में से क्या नहीं पाया गया था?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: आवास गृह
सार्वजनिक स्नान गृह
सार्वजनिक अस्पताल
सार्वजनिक भवन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सार्वजनिक अस्पताल

Explanation:
हड़प्पा सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) एक उन्नत नगरीय सभ्यता थी, जिसमें आवास गृह, सार्वजनिक स्नानागार (जैसे मोहनजोदड़ो का 'महान स्नानागार'), और सार्वजनिक भवन (जैसे अन्नागार) पाए गए थे। हालांकि, सार्वजनिक अस्पतालों के कोई साक्ष्य नहीं मिले हैं। हड़प्पावासी स्वच्छता और नगर नियोजन में उन्नत थे, लेकिन चिकित्सा सुविधाओं के बारे में कोई प्रत्यक्ष प्रमाण नहीं है।

Extra Facts:
हड़प्पा सभ्यता को 'सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता' भी कहा जाता है। यह सभ्यता व्यापार, मुहरों, और माप-तौल की प्रणाली के लिए प्रसिद्ध थी। हड़प्पावासी कांस्य युग के थे और उन्होंने लिपि का उपयोग किया, जो अभी तक पढ़ी नहीं जा सकी है। मोहनजोदड़ो और हड़प्पा इस सभ्यता के प्रमुख स्थल हैं।

question:
The word India came from the Indus, called ______ in Sanskrit.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Bhanuh
Adya
Sarvatr
Sindhu
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sindhu

Explanation:
The word India is derived from the river Indus, which is called 'Sindhu' in Sanskrit. In ancient times, the Greeks and Persians referred to this river as 'Indos' or 'Hindu', which later evolved into the term 'India'. The Indus River is one of the major rivers of the Indian subcontinent and is mentioned in the Rigveda. It was the cradle of the Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE), one of the world's oldest urban civilizations.

Extra Facts:
The Indus River now flows through Pakistan, but in ancient times, it was a vital part of Indian culture and civilization. The Rigveda refers to it as 'Sindhu'. The Indus Valley Civilization, which flourished along its banks, was renowned for its advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and trade networks.

Expected Questions for Upcoming Exams :
☛ Indus Valley Civilization - Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro were its major cities.
☛ Rigveda - Mentions the Sindhu River.
☛ Indos - Greek name for the Indus River.
☛ Hindu - Persian term for the Sindhu River.
☛ Bharat - The Constitution of India recognizes both 'India' and 'Bharat' as official names.
question_hi:
इण्डिया शब्द इण्डस से आया है, जिसे संस्कृत में___________कहा जाता है।

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: भानुः
अद्य
सर्वत्र
सिंधु
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है सिंधु

Explanation:
इण्डिया शब्द की उत्पत्ति इण्डस नदी से हुई है, जिसे संस्कृत में 'सिंधु' कहा जाता है। प्राचीन काल में यूनानी और फारसी लोगों ने इस नदी को 'इंडोस' या 'हिंदू' कहा, जिससे बाद में 'इंडिया' शब्द बना। सिंधु नदी भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप की एक प्रमुख नदी है और इसका ऋग्वेद में भी उल्लेख मिलता है। यह नदी प्राचीन सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) का केंद्र थी, जो विश्व की प्राचीनतम नगरीय सभ्यताओं में से एक है।

Extra Facts:
सिंधु नदी वर्तमान में पाकिस्तान से होकर बहती है, लेकिन प्राचीन काल में यह भारतीय संस्कृति और सभ्यता का महत्वपूर्ण अंग थी। ऋग्वेद में इसे 'सिंधु' के नाम से संबोधित किया गया है। इस नदी के किनारे विकसित हुई सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता अपनी उन्नत नगर योजना, जल निकासी व्यवस्था और व्यापार के लिए प्रसिद्ध थी।

☛ ऋग्वेद - सिंधु नदी का उल्लेख इस वेद में मिलता है।

☛ हिंदू - फारसियों द्वारा सिंधु नदी को कहा जाता था।
☛ भारत - संविधान में आधिकारिक नाम 'इंडिया' के साथ-साथ 'भारत' भी है।

question:
Which of the following cities existed in the Indus Valley Civilization?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Harappa
Sanchi
Muziris
Ayodhya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Harappa

Explanation:
The Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) was an ancient urban civilization spread across present-day Pakistan and northwestern India. Harappa was one of its major cities, located in Punjab, Pakistan. Discovered in 1921, the civilization is named after this site. Harappa showcases advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and large granaries. Other options like Sanchi (Mauryan-era Buddhist stupa), Muziris (ancient Roman trading port), and Ayodhya (Ramayana-era city) are unrelated to the Indus Valley Civilization.

Extra Facts:
The Indus Valley Civilization is also called the Harappan Civilization. Other key cities include Mohenjo-Daro (Sindh, Pakistan), Dholavira (Gujarat, India), and Lothal (Gujarat, India). Known for its seals, standardized weights, and trade networks, its script remains undeciphered.

☛ Dholavira - Famous for water conservation systems (Gujarat)
☛ Lothal - Ancient port city with dockyard evidence
☛ Kalibangan - Evidence of ploughed fields (Rajasthan)
☛ Ropar - Shows transition between Indus and Vedic cultures (Punjab, India)

Explanation:
सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) एक प्राचीन नगरीय सभ्यता थी जो वर्तमान पाकिस्तान और उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत में फैली हुई थी। हड़प्पा इस सभ्यता का एक प्रमुख शहर था, जो पाकिस्तान के पंजाब प्रांत में स्थित है। यह स्थल सबसे पहले 1921 में खोजा गया था और इसी के नाम पर इस सभ्यता का नाम 'हड़प्पा सभ्यता' पड़ा। इस शहर में उन्नत नगर नियोजन, जल निकासी व्यवस्था और विशाल अन्नागार के साक्ष्य मिले हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे साँची (मौर्य कालीन बौद्ध स्तूप), मुज़िरिस (प्राचीन रोमन व्यापारिक केंद्र), और अयोध्या (रामायण कालीन नगरी) सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता से संबंधित नहीं हैं।

question:
Which material was used to make beads in the Harappan Civilisation?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Wood
Plastic
Limestone
Carnelian stone
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Carnelian stone

Explanation:
In the Harappan Civilisation (2600-1900 BCE), carnelian stone was widely used for making beads. It is a semi-precious stone found in red and orange hues. The Harappans crafted beautiful beads by cutting, grinding, and polishing carnelian. These beads were used for trade and ornamentation. Evidence of carnelian beads has been found at sites like Mohenjo-Daro and Lothal, confirming their usage.

Extra Facts:
Other materials used for bead-making in the Harappan Civilisation included shell, gold, copper, faience (a type of glass), and agate. The Harappans drilled holes in beads using drilling machines, showcasing their advanced technical skills.

कारेलियन पत्थर

Explanation:
हड़प्पा सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) में मोतियों को बनाने के लिए कारेलियन पत्थर का व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता था। यह एक अर्ध-कीमती पत्थर है जिसे लाल और नारंगी रंगों में पाया जाता है। हड़प्पावासी इसे काटकर, घिसकर और पॉलिश करके सुंदर मोती बनाते थे। ये मोती व्यापार और आभूषण दोनों के लिए प्रयोग किए जाते थे। मोहनजोदड़ो और लोथल जैसे स्थलों से कारेलियन के मोती प्राप्त हुए हैं, जो इसके उपयोग के प्रमाण हैं।

question:
In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the __________ directions.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: anonymous
cardinal
ordinal
incognito
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cardinal

Explanation:
The Harappan civilisation (2600-1900 BCE) had meticulously planned cities with streets aligned along the cardinal directions (north-south, east-west). This grid-based urban planning facilitated efficient drainage, ventilation, and trade activities. Major sites like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa exhibit this advanced system, reflecting their engineering prowess.

Extra Facts:

question:
Which of the following sites of Harappan civilization is located near Bolan Pass?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Mehrgarh
Chirand
Gufkral
Koldihwa
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mehrgarh

Explanation:
Mehrgarh is a significant archaeological site of the Harappan civilization located near the Bolan Pass. Situated in Balochistan, Pakistan, it provides evidence of continuous habitation from the Neolithic period (7000 BCE) to the Harappan era (2500 BCE). This site was a major center for early agriculture, animal domestication, and metallurgy. Findings of wheat, barley, and cotton cultivation highlight its economic importance in the development of the Harappan civilization.

Extra Facts:
Mehrgarh is often referred to as the 'precursor to the Harappan civilization' due to its cultural continuity with later Indus Valley sites. The inhabitants produced pottery, beads, and copper tools. Discovered in 1974 by French archaeologist Jean-François Jarrige, this site offers crucial insights into early urbanization in South Asia.

question:
In which of the following Indian states, Harappan cities have NOT been found?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Uttarakhand
Gujarat
Rajasthan
Haryana
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Uttarakhand

Explanation:
The Harappan Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) was the earliest urban civilization of the Indian subcontinent. Its remains have been found mainly in the Indus River Valley and surrounding regions. Gujarat (Lothal, Dholavira), Rajasthan (Kalibangan), and Haryana (Rakhigarhi, Banawali) have evidence of Harappan cities. However, no Harappan site has been discovered in Uttarakhand so far, as this region is far from the main Indus Valley and located in the Himalayan foothills, where urbanization evidence is absent.

Extra Facts:
The Harappan Civilization , also called the 'Indus Valley Civilization', is famous for its advanced town planning, drainage systems, and cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa. Dholavira (Gujarat) is the only Harappan site with an advanced water conservation system. The decline of this civilization around 1900 BCE is attributed to climate change and river course shifts.

question:
Which method was used for making bronze statues during Harappan Civilisation?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Lost wax casting
Ivory carving
Stone carving
Wood carving
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lost wax casting

Explanation:
During the Harappan Civilisation (2600-1900 BCE), the 'Lost Wax Casting' method was used to create bronze statues. In this technique, a wax model was coated with clay and heated, causing the wax to melt away, leaving a hollow mold. Molten metal was then poured into this mold to create the statue. A famous example is the 'Dancing Girl' statue found in Mohenjo-Daro, showcasing the advanced metallurgical skills of the Harappans. This method highlights their expertise in metalwork and artistic craftsmanship.

Extra Facts:
The Harappan Civilisation, also called the Indus Valley Civilisation, was one of the earliest urban cultures. They mastered the use of copper, tin, and bronze to create beads, utensils, tools, and weapons. Standardized weights and measures and seals were other notable features. Their cities had well-planned drainage systems.

The Great Bath of Mohenjo-Daro is a rectangular structure showcasing the advanced engineering skills of the Indus Valley Civilization (circa 2500 BCE). The Harappan Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) primarily obtained copper from present-day Rajasthan, specifically the Khetri and Khera regions. These areas were rich in copper deposits, which the Harappans used to make tools, ornaments, and other artifacts. Copper was alloyed with tin to produce bronze, a hallmark of the Harappan culture. While some copper was also sourced from Balochistan (modern-day Pakistan), Rajasthan remained the major supplier within the Indian subcontinent.

Extra Facts:
The Harappan Civilization is often referred to as a Bronze Age civilization due to its advanced metallurgical skills. Excavations at Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa have revealed copper vessels, knives, and figurines. Additionally, the Harappans engaged in trade to acquire metals from other regions.

question:
Which of the following types of house remains were found in Mehrgarh site of Harappan civilization?

options: Triangular or circular
Rectangular or circular
Square or rectangular
Circular or square
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Square or rectangular

Explanation:
The Mehrgarh archaeological site (located in present-day Pakistan) of the Harappan civilization has revealed remains of square and rectangular houses. This site dates back to 7000 BCE and is considered a precursor to the Harappan civilization. The houses were made of mud bricks and had separate rooms, indicating that the people of that time had knowledge of permanent settlements and social organization. Mehrgarh is also known as an early center of agriculture and animal domestication.

Extra Facts:
Mehrgarh is regarded as the 'initial phase' of the Harappan civilization. Evidence of wheat, barley, and cotton cultivation has been found here. Additionally, artifacts such as pottery, beads, and metal tools have been discovered. This site belongs to the Neolithic period, and its people used wheel-made pottery.

Balathal

Dholavira is a major Harappan site located in the Kutch district of Gujarat. It was one of the largest and most significant cities of the Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE). Discovered in 1967-68 by J.P. Joshi, Dholavira is renowned for its advanced water management system, massive fortifications, and well-planned urban layout. The inscriptions and symbols found here have contributed significantly to understanding the Harappan script. Dholavira has also been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Extra Facts:
Other prominent sites of the Harappan civilization include Mohenjo-Daro (Pakistan), Harappa (Pakistan), Lothal (Gujarat), and Kalibangan (Rajasthan). The reservoirs and canals found at Dholavira showcase the advanced engineering skills of this civilization. Artifacts such as beads, metal objects, and pottery found here reflect the trade and craftsmanship of the Harappan period.

question:
The famous Indus Valley site Mohenjo - daro was first excavated by the eminent Indian archaeologist.

[RRB NTPC CBT]

R D Banerji
Daya Ram Sahni
SR Rao
solution:

Explanation:
Rakhal Das Banerji (R.D. Banerji) excavated Mohenjo-daro in 1922. He was a prominent archaeologist of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and was the first to identify this site as belonging to an ancient civilization. Mohenjo-daro, meaning 'Mound of the Dead', was a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization and is now located in Sindh, Pakistan. Banerji's discovery played a crucial role in uncovering details about the Harappan Civilization.

Extra Facts:
The Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations. Other key sites include Harappa (Pakistan), Dholavira (Gujarat), and Kalibangan (Rajasthan). The script of this civilization remains undeciphered. The town planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures reflect an advanced society for its time.

question:
On the bank of which river was Harappa City situated?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Satluj river

Bhogwa river

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ravi river

Explanation:
The ancient city of Harappa , a major center of the Indus Valley Civilization, was situated on the banks of the Ravi river . This river flows through the Punjab province of present-day Pakistan. During the Harappan era (2600-1900 BCE), this city was a significant trade and cultural hub. The proximity to the Ravi river provided favorable conditions for agriculture, water supply, and transportation. The site was discovered in 1921 by Dayaram Sahni .

Extra Facts:
The Harappan Civilization is also called the 'Indus Valley Civilization' because it flourished along the Indus River and its tributaries. Other major cities of this civilization include Mohenjo-Daro (Indus River), Dholavira (Gujarat), and Kalibangan (Ghaggar River) . The Harappans were known for urban planning, drainage systems, and seals.

question:
What is the name of the earliest form of writing known in the Indian subcontinent?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Pali Script
Indus Script
Brahmi Script
Sanskrit Script
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indus Script

Explanation:
The Indus Script is the earliest known form of writing in the Indian subcontinent, used during the Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE). It primarily appears on seals, pottery, and other artifacts. Despite extensive research, this script remains undeciphered, leaving its language and meaning a mystery. The script is written from right to left and consists of over 400 symbols. Its existence indicates a sophisticated urban culture with trade, craft, and administrative systems.

Extra Facts:
After the Indus Script, the Brahmi Script (3rd century BCE) emerged, becoming the foundation for modern Indian scripts like Devanagari, Tamil, and Telugu. The Indus Valley Civilization, associated with this script, was a highly advanced society with planned cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa, showcasing early urban development in South Asia.

Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?

[SSC MTS 2022]

Aegean civilization

Explanation:

Major cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa featured grid-patterned streets, baked-brick houses, and an advanced drainage system connected to each household. This system was one of the most remarkable engineering feats of its time.

Artifacts such as seals, statues, and jewelry reflect its rich cultural heritage. The decline of this civilization around 1900 BCE is attributed to factors like climate change, river course shifts, and economic decline.

question:

Explanation:
The ancient city of Harappa was built on the bank of the now-dry course of the Ravi River in present-day Punjab, Pakistan. The Ravi River provided essential water resources and fertile soil, making Harappa a prosperous trade hub.

Extra Facts:
The Indus Valley Civilization, also called the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban cultures. Other key cities included Mohenjo-Daro (on the Indus River), Dholavira (Gujarat), and Lothal. Harappans were renowned for urban planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights.

question:

[RRB ALP CBT]

Ayyappa

solution:

Explanation:
The people of the Indus Valley Civilisation (2600-1900 BCE) worshipped Pashupati. This claim is based on the 'Pashupati Seal' discovered at Mohenjo-Daro, depicting a deity seated in a yogic posture surrounded by animals (elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, buffalo). Extra Facts:
Religious practices in the Indus Valley Civilisation have limited evidence, but key elements include worship of Mother Goddess, tree worship (peepal), and animal worship (bull). Seals and figurines from Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa help decode their beliefs.

Explanation:
सुरकोतड़ा एक महत्वपूर्ण सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता का पुरातात्विक स्थल है, जो गुजरात राज्य के कच्छ जिले में स्थित है। यह स्थल 1964 में जे.पी. जोशी द्वारा खोजा गया था। यहाँ से घोड़े की हड्डियों के साक्ष्य मिले हैं, जो संभवतः हड़प्पा काल में घोड़ों के उपयोग का संकेत देते हैं। सुरकोतड़ा की खुदाई से किलेबंदी, आवासीय भवन, और मिट्टी के बर्तन जैसी संरचनाएँ प्राप्त हुई हैं, जो इस सभ्यता की उन्नत नगर योजना को दर्शाती हैं।

Extra Facts:
सुरकोतड़ा को हड़प्पा सभ्यता के परिपक्व चरण (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) का माना जाता है। यहाँ मिले मिट्टी के खिलौने, मोहरें, और तांबे की वस्तुएँ इस सभ्यता के आर्थिक और सांस्कृतिक विकास को दर्शाते हैं। इसके अलावा, यह स्थल हड़प्पा और मोहनजोदड़ो जैसे प्रमुख केंद्रों से व्यापारिक संबंध रखता था।
